inherits.lag2_panel: same denominator-separated t performance -> t+1 to t+2 adult-count interval used in PALMER_PERFORMANCE_REDISTRIBUTION_LAGS_RESULT_V2

known_before_freeze: Past relative reproductive performance S_i,t positively predicts relative breeder-count growth during t+1 to t+2 under the fixed lag-2 specification.
Measured reproductive performance has weak one-year memory, and past S_i,t retains incremental information after S_i,t+1.
Colony counts cannot uniquely separate attendance, mature-bird movement and first recruitment.

External Ross Island work shows successful breeders can have higher subsequent survival/reproductive performance, making resident-quality persistence a serious alternative to social-information settlement.
question: Is the Palmer lag-2 performance association carried mainly by avoidance of breeder loss, by positive net addition of breeding pairs, or by both?

biological_competing_mechanisms.retention_quality: High S_i,t marks colonies containing successful/high-quality resident breeders that are more likely to survive, attend and continue breeding; this should primarily reduce subsequent losses and does not require net entry.
biological_competing_mechanisms.entry_reentry: High S_i,t is associated with later addition of breeding pairs not observed breeding at that colony at the start of the outcome interval; this may arise from first recruitment, return from a nonbreeding state, or immigration/prospecting.
biological_competing_mechanisms.important_boundary: Positive net addition does not distinguish first recruitment, return from skipped breeding, or immigration and is not by itself evidence of public-information use.

outcome_interval.N0: adult breeding-pair count at colony i in t+1
outcome_interval.N1: adult breeding-pair count at colony i in t+2

derived_responses.loss_avoidance: Aminus = -Gminus, so a positive coefficient means high prior performance is associated with less later loss
derived_responses.net_new_pairs_lower_bound: Lplus = max(N1 - N0, 0); whenever Lplus > 0, at least Lplus breeding pairs at t+2 were not part of the observed breeding-pair count at that colony at t+1, regardless of simultaneous exits

risk_set_adjustment.within_island_transition: For each island and t+1 -> t+2 transition, demean Gplus and Aminus across eligible colony codes.
risk_set_adjustment.prior_size_control: z-standardize log1p(N0) within the same island-transition risk set.
risk_set_adjustment.reason: This matches the lag-2 architecture while separating positive and negative demographic components.

primary_models.gain: demeaned_Gplus ~ beta_gain * S_i,t + z_log_size_i,t+1 + island:colony_code fixed effect
primary_models.loss_avoidance: demeaned_Aminus ~ beta_avoid * S_i,t + z_log_size_i,t+1 + island:colony_code fixed effect

inference.null: Within each predictor island-season, colony assignment of S_i,t is exchangeable while outcome counts, missingness, prior size and colony identities remain fixed.
inference.permutation: Use the full eligible predictor island-season S_i,t group exactly as in the corrected performance-memory implementation; map each permutation onto the fixed lag-2 outcome panel by colony.
inference.p_values: one-sided upper-tail for beta_gain and beta_avoid
inference.multiple_testing: Holm-adjust the two primary p-values; mechanism support requires adjusted p <= 0.05 and coefficient > 0.

logical_lower_bound_test.statistic: Among lag-2 rows with positive net change, report total and median Lplus and the fraction of all positive-growth rows with Lplus > 0 (algebraically 1 by definition).
logical_lower_bound_test.performance_link: Fit demeaned log1p(Lplus) with S_i,t + within-transition z_log_size + colony fixed effects, assigning log1p(0)=0 before demeaning.
logical_lower_bound_test.role: secondary support showing whether prior performance predicts a strict lower bound on entry/re-entry; does not identify its source.
logical_lower_bound_test.inference: same within-predictor-island-season permutation, one-sided p reported descriptively without replacing the two primary endpoints

decision_matrix.retention_dominant_pattern: beta_avoid supported after Holm; beta_gain not supported.
decision_matrix.entry_dominant_pattern: beta_gain supported after Holm; beta_avoid not supported.
decision_matrix.mixed_pattern: both beta_gain and beta_avoid supported after Holm.
decision_matrix.retention_only_ruled_out: true only if beta_gain is supported after Holm; this means some performance-linked advantage occurs through positive net breeder additions, not that retention contributes nothing.

sensitivities.exclude_litchfield: Repeat both primary coefficients and raw p-values excluding LIT.
sensitivities.minimum_prior_size_2: Repeat after requiring N0 >= 2 breeding pairs.
sensitivities.alternate_logratio_performance: Repeat using the frozen logratio performance state.
sensitivities.leave_one_island_out: Report observed beta_gain and beta_avoid after removing each island.

claim_boundaries: Do not call Lplus immigration; it is net addition from any pair not observed breeding at that colony at t+1, including returning nonbreeders and first recruits.
Do not infer public-information use from a supported gain component.
Do not infer resident individual quality from a supported loss-avoidance component.
Do not alter the lag, gain/loss decomposition, controls, alpha, multiplicity rule or permutation scheme after outcomes are opened.
This analysis can rule out a pure retention-only account if gain is supported, but it cannot identify which entry pathway supplies the added breeders.
